newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE SHOULD ADOPT A STRICT INCOMES POLICY-SPRAOS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE SHOULD ADOPT A STRICT INCOMES POLICY-SPRAOS.

text.p: Greece should adhere to a strict incomes policy to achieve EU convergence, economics professor Yiannis Spraos told financial weekly Ekonomikos Tahydromos.
Spraos is an advisor to the Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis and heads a committee of economic experts.
The committee's report, released last week, called for tough incomes and fiscal policies for the next two years, including a one-off 10 percent tax on corporate earnings.
"It (the 10 percent charge) was a proposal of marginal importance in relation to the proposed incomes policy," he said.

The overwhelming press emphasis on the surcharge was unjustified said Spraos who called its outright rejection by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou proof of 'the independent role of the committee'.
"The primary principle which we must adopt from here on in is simple: an increase in real incomes must coincide with an increase in the average productivity of the economy," said Spraos.
A compensatory amount for inflation would also be calculated into this figure, he added.

"The entire issue depends on the decisiveness of the government, which must clearly say to social partners: 'Sirs, the economy and the convergence programme allows wage increases of up to 4.0 percent. Choose," said Spraos.

"Workers and trade union organisations must understand that under conditions of low inflation, nominally small increases can mean an increase in their real income, and not a reduction." --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
